key_insight: Standalone CNNs delivered the best dense breast tissue segmentation and accuracy–compute balance, outperforming transformers and CNN-prompted MedSAM under limited annotation.
clinical_relevance: More accurate dense-tissue segmentation could support breast-density assessment in mammography, where dense tissue can obscure cancers and is associated with increased breast cancer risk.
method: Compared classical methods, CNN/U-Net models, transformers, and prompt-based MedSAM.
Evaluated self-supervised pretraining, fine-tuning strategies, and loss functions.
Tested box, breast-region, and CNN-generated dense prompts for MedSAM.
evidence_signal: Using 596 expert-annotated images and 20,000 unlabeled mammograms under a unified evaluation protocol, a density-calibrated hybrid loss reduced percent-density test MAE from 14.8 to 11.8 percentage points.
watch_item: MedSAM performance depended strongly on prompt quality, and mask-decoder fine-tuning did not make it outperform the best standalone CNN.
paper_title: Dense Breast Tissue Segmentation under Limited Annotation: Comparing CNNs, Transformers, Self-Supervision, and Prompting
